problem: The raw DWG modeler writer accepted an AcDs byte array with an ACIS BinaryFile marker at an arbitrary offset. The same bytes would not pass the dwg2dxf modeler projection's prefix check, and the reader only identifies the payload as SAB when the signature starts at byte zero.

authority.source: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
authority.finding: The SAB stream is prefixed with ACIS BinaryFile; raw DataStorage records may contain other opaque data, so the rule is applied only when admitting a REGION/3DSOLID as a modeler carrier.

physicalSourceObservations.source: ODA 27.1 generated AC1027 three-solid drawing from locally authored DXF
physicalSourceObservations.records: schema-1 handles 0x8A, 0x8B, and 0x8C all have the marker at payload offset zero

physicalSourceObservations.source: public AC1027 example drawing, provenance in p5-ac1027-tablegeometry-null-cell-cache-transport-2026-11-01.json
physicalSourceObservations.records: schema-1 handles 0x176, 0x37D, and 0x2E1 all have the marker at payload offset zero

implementation: The fixed-modeler raw replay preflight and its finalization both require marker offset zero. Other DataStorage records and generic marker scanning retain their existing opaque behavior.

validation.coverage: A generated two-page blob whose marker crosses a page boundary is refused as a modeler payload without altering a destination sentinel. Adding the prefix to the same payload and section permits same-writer retry and typed modeler/blob readback; opaque scanning of interior markers remains covered by existing DataStorage controls.

limitations: The prefix is necessary framing, not proof that the following bytes encode a valid SAB or that an independent kernel accepts them.
The physical records were inspected, not replayed through the writer or checked for native geometric semantics.
